text: {"claims":[{"claim_text":"By default the kubelet sends HTTP/2 requests for HTTP probes.","verdict":"CONTRADICTED","reasoning":"Passage 0 states the default is HTTP/1.1, not HTTP/2.","citations":[{"index":0,"quote":"By default the `kubelet` sends HTTP/1.1 requests when executing an HTTP probe."}]},{"claim_text":"Using HTTP/1.1 instead requires the H2CContainerProbe feature gate.","verdict":"CONTRADICTED","reasoning":"Passage 0 states HTTP/1.1 is the default and the H2CContainerProbe gate is required for using HTTP/2 cleartext (h2c) in probes.","citations":[{"index":0,"quote":"By default the `kubelet` sends HTTP/1.1 requests when executing an HTTP probe."},{"index":0,"quote":"This requires the `H2CContainerProbe` [feature gate](/docs/reference/command-line-tools-reference/feature-gates/) to be enabled on both the `kube-apiserver` and the `kubelet`."}]},{"claim_text":"A TCP probe considers the container healthy if it can open a socket on the given port.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 1 says the kubelet attempts to open a socket on the specified port and that a successful connection means the container is healthy.","citations":[{"index":1,"quote":"the kubelet will attempt to open a socket to your container on the specified port. If it can establish a connection, the container is considered healthy"}]},{"claim_text":"If the readiness probe fails, the kubelet restarts the container.","verdict":"UNSUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 2 says a failed readiness probe marks the pod unready and prevents traffic; it does not state that the kubelet restarts the container.","citations":[]},{"claim_text":"gRPC probes connect over TLS by default.","verdict":"CONTRADICTED","reasoning":"Passage 4 states gRPC health endpoints are connected to over plaintext by default.","citations":[{"index":4,"quote":"By default the `kubelet` connects to gRPC health endpoints over plaintext."}]},{"claim_text":"In TLS mode the kubelet verifies the server certificate.","verdict":"CONTRADICTED","reasoning":"Passage 5 states that in TLS mode the kubelet uses InsecureSkipVerify and does not verify the server certificate.","citations":[{"index":5,"quote":"When `mode` is set to `TLS`, the `kubelet` connects over TLS with `InsecureSkipVerify` and does not verify the server certificate."}]},{"claim_text":"The timeoutSeconds setting defaults to 1 second.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 3 states that the timeoutSeconds setting defaults to 1s.","citations":[{"index":3,"quote":"the `timeoutSeconds` setting (which defaults to 1s)"}]},{"claim_text":"If a startup probe never succeeds, the container keeps running.","verdict":"CONTRADICTED","reasoning":"Passage 6 states that if the startup probe never succeeds, the container is killed after 300s.","citations":[{"index":6,"quote":"If the startup probe never succeeds, the container is killed after 300s and subject to the pod's `restartPolicy`."}]},{"claim_text":"If a startup probe never succeeds, the container is never marked ready.","verdict":"UNSUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 6 says the container is killed after 300s if the startup probe never succeeds, but it does not state anything about being marked ready.","citations":[]},{"claim_text":"Readiness probes only start after the liveness probe has succeeded.","verdict":"CONTRADICTED","reasoning":"Passage 8 states that readiness and liveness probes do not depend on each other to succeed.","citations":[{"index":8,"quote":"The readiness and liveness probes do not depend on each other to succeed."}]}]}
